I added `is_valid_username` to `lnbits/helpers.py`, but the test run needs your approval, so I haven't run the function on any inputs. The pcat check on the code reported no deviations.

I built it from the catalog's `validators.regex_match` pattern and kept its `# pcat: validators.regex_match@v1` marker. It requires 2–20 characters of letters, digits, dots and underscores. The name can't start or end with `.` or `_`, and it can't contain two separators in a row (`..`, `__`, `._` or `_.`).

From reading the regex, I think a name with a trailing newline (`"ab\n"`) would pass. The `$` in the lookahead matches before a final newline, and the `[^_.]` at the end accepts `\n`. If usernames come from raw input, strip the string first. I haven't confirmed this. Changing it means leaving the reviewed pattern, so I haven't touched it. If you want that fixed, tell me and I'll make the change and propose a `pcat-allow` line. A human would have to confirm that line in the pull request.

input.code:
import re

# pcat: validators.regex_match@v1
def is_valid_username(username: str) -> bool:
    username_regex = "(?=[a-zA-Z0-9._]{2,20}$)(?!.*[_.]{2})[^_.].*[^_.]"
    return re.fullmatch(username_regex, username) is not None
